title: Patterns in text
description:
Use the `re` module for four jobs:

```python
def find_emails(text): ...         # sorted, distinct, lower-cased addresses found anywhere in the text
def to_iso_dates(text): ...        # every DD/MM/YYYY date rewritten as YYYY-MM-DD; the rest unchanged
def is_hex_colour(text): ...       # "#1a2B3c" or "#fff": a # and exactly 3 or 6 hex digits, nothing else
def parse_log(line): ...           # dict with date, time, level, message; None if the line does not fit
```

- An email here is: one or more of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `%`, `+`, `-`; an `@`; then one or more parts of letters, digits and `-` separated by dots, ending in a dot and 2 or more letters.
- Dates have 1 or 2 digit days and months: `5/1/2026` becomes `2026-01-05` (pad with zeros).
- Log lines look like `2026-11-15 10:42:07 ERROR disk full`: a date, a time, a level of capital letters, and a message (the rest, at least one character).
hints: `re.sub` accepts a function as the replacement: it receives the match object and returns the new text, which lets you reorder and pad the groups.
Use `re.fullmatch` when the **whole** string must have the form; `search` and `findall` find it anywhere.
